memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: For seven days celebrate the festival to the Lord your God at the place the Lord will choose. For the Lord your God will bless you in all your harvest and in all the work of your hands, and your joy will be complete. - Deut 16:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells His people that when they honour Him and gather to celebrate, their "joy will be complete." What a promise. God is not against our happiness. He is its true source. When the people rested from their labour and rejoiced in Him, they discovered a fullness they could never find in the harvest itself.

The blessing came "in all your harvest and in all the work of your hands," yet the completeness of joy was found before the Lord, not merely in the goods gathered. The stuff was good, but God Himself was the joy. That is a distinction we easily lose.

We often chase complete joy in achievements, possessions, or experiences, only to find them strangely empty once we have them. This verse gently corrects us. Full joy is found in God's presence, not in His gifts alone. Jesus said He came so that our joy might be complete, and that this joy is found in abiding in His love (John 15:11). The harvest fades, but the God we rejoice in never fails. If you feel a hollowness even in good seasons, it may be that your heart was made to find its fullest joy in Him. Where are you looking for complete joy today?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you looked for joy that left you empty?
2. What would it mean to find complete joy in God's presence?
3. How can you abide in Christ's love this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are the true source of my joy. Draw me close, that my joy may be complete in You. Amen.
